rationale: Round 0 built and validated cleanly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises SecurityGain and DiversityGain across all seven passes while keeping RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights capped near 0.5 to bound overhead on this small (14 KB text) but loop-heavy C++ benchmark. SUB is nearly free and semantically safe, so it gets the strongest pull; SPLIT stays cheap and composes well by enlarging basic-block counts that FLA and BCF then scramble. FLA and BCF are pushed higher than round 0 since correctness held, but their runtime weights stay below their security weights because the hottest functions (_ZSt16__introsort_loop, _Z10deque_testPdS_i, list/copy_move loops) are iteration-dense, so flattening and bogus-control-flow dispatch would multiply inner-loop cost if over-applied. IBR and ICALL are held at moderate runtime cost since indirect branches and calls in template-heavy recursive code (introsort, power) can thrash the branch predictor and defeat inlining; their CorrectnessRisk is the highest here because opaque indirect targets in vtable/exception-heavy C++ can interact with unwinding. IGV stays enabled at moderate weight to diversify global-variable layout across the five translation units, aiding diversity without touching per-function hot paths.
